source.title: Deep Learning with Zero Initialization: Revisiting Symmetry Breaking and Gradient Flow

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether zero initialization permits learning and reports cases where it stalls or learns with added node noise or residual connections. It does not measure the training classification error named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The reported benchmark tables give mean accuracy, and the figures describe accuracy trajectories; these are not training-error measurements. The explicit statements about whether learning proceeds are recorded below. Cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study measures learnability and accuracy under zero, mixed and random initialization. It does not test near-zero training error, width-dependent local minima, depth degradation, activation-matched signal-preserving initialization, learning-rate stability or batch-normalization acceleration. Its qualitative reports of faster early accuracy gains concern different initialization schemes and do not establish V4's specified mechanism.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors conclude that zero initialization need not prevent learning when gradient diversity is supplied, and that zero or mixed initialization can sometimes match or exceed default initialization. They do not claim universal performance improvement and acknowledge missing rigorous proofs and gradient-dynamics analyses.
record.recipe_differences: Studies zero and mixed initialization schemes rather than the claim versions' training-error, width, depth, learning-rate, or batch-normalization recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Consecutive zero-initialized layers stall learning; node noise and residual connections enable learning. The text also says zero-initializing early layers can reduce accuracy in some settings.

fits_no_version.finding: All-zero CNNs fail to learn; node noise or residual connections enable above-chance accuracy. Residual and default CNNs differ in architecture and size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning from all-zero initialization can become possible when activation diversity is supplied through noise or suitable residual connections.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 5.2 and Appendix C report faster early accuracy improvements under some zero-initialization settings, while acknowledging possible dependence on the final accuracy ceiling.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Zero-initializing selected layers can accelerate early accuracy gains relative to default initialization under some tested recipes.

record.problems: The study reports test accuracy rather than training classification error for its benchmark comparisons. It states that it lacks a rigorous mathematical proof and omits statistical analyses of weight statistics and gradient magnitudes.
record.rows_left_out: No benchmark accuracy values or accuracy-trajectory figures were extracted as rows because they do not measure training classification error. Appendix tables contain many initialization-condition accuracies, likewise not the claim's measure.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error from random initialization, including corrupted labels and dependence on size, stopping or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with increasing depth, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified deep-network alternatives.
Activation-matched signal and gradient preservation, its effects on speed and trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Recovery or divergence relative to a learning-rate stability threshold and associated curvature dynamics.
Controlled normalization comparisons of training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The record's tests/T5 classification conflicts with its finding that no version is tested. Benchmark accuracies are selected test-set peaks according to Appendix B.5. Figures 2–4 nevertheless call their trajectories training accuracy; this terminology conflict should be preserved rather than resolved by assumption. The supplied text contains no readable trajectory values establishing near-zero training error. States of cannot_determine above concern the claim versions, not uncertainty about the authors' stated learnability outcomes.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima, and the effect of student width.
Depth-related degradation in plain networks and whether identity shortcuts prevent it.
Activation-matched initialization, learning speed comparisons for Gaussian versus orthogonal weights, and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability limits, loss curvature, and sharpness.
Batch-normalization speed and learning-rate tolerance comparisons, and Fixup training without normalization.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Train with all weights and biases initialized to zero.
rows.note: The paper explicitly says learning does not proceed under this initialization.
rows.check: The reported failure to learn is accurate; Table 1 gives 11.35% test accuracy. It does not measure an effect specified by a claim version.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Train with all weights and biases initialized to zero.
rows.note: The paper explicitly says learning does not proceed under this initialization.
rows.check: The reported failure to learn is accurate; Table 1 gives 10.00% test accuracy. All-zero initialization is outside V1's random-initialization condition.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Train with all weights and biases initialized to zero.
rows.note: The paper explicitly says learning does not proceed under this initialization.
rows.check: The reported failure to learn is accurate; Table 1 gives 1.00% test accuracy. All-zero initialization is outside V1's random-initialization condition.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Train with all weights and biases initialized to zero and residual connections.
rows.note: The paper reports that learning can occur with residual connections.
rows.check: Learning occurs, with 91.77% test accuracy. The residual CNN has a different architecture and parameter count from the default CNN; this is not a controlled test of depth degradation or its prevention.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Train with all weights and biases initialized to zero and residual connections.
rows.note: The paper reports that learning can occur with residual connections.
rows.check: Learning occurs, with 35.03% test accuracy. The residual CNN has a different architecture and parameter count from the default CNN; no depth sweep or training-error comparison tests V3.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Train with all weights and biases initialized to zero and residual connections.
rows.note: The paper reports that learning can occur with residual connections.
rows.check: Learning occurs, with 10.79% test accuracy. Residual connections enabling learning from zero initialization do not test V3's depth-degradation claim.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Train with all weights and biases initialized to zero and noise injected into nodes.
rows.note: The paper reports that learning can occur with node noise.
rows.check: Learning occurs, with 99.10% test accuracy, but this does not establish any version's specified effect. Noise supplies initial activation diversity rather than remaining an unconditional intervention throughout training.

rows.subject: CNNs
rows.operation_detail: Train with all weights and biases initialized to zero and noise injected into nodes.
rows.note: The paper reports that learning can occur with node noise.
rows.check: Learning occurs, with 70.03% test accuracy. Algorithm 2 injects noise conditionally while a layer's weights remain entirely zero; this does not measure V4's activation-matched signal-preserving initialization.

rows.note: The paper reports that learning can occur with node noise.
rows.check: Learning occurs, with 36.19% test accuracy, but this does not establish any version's specified effect. Noise supplies initial activation diversity rather than remaining an unconditional intervention throughout training.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
